methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $20M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Amperon is a Series B–stage infrastructure and logistics company founded by Sean Kelly that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis operates without access to direct public comparables or identified private peer benchmarks in the infrastructure and logistics sector, limiting the ability to triangulate via traditional multiples-based approaches.

Given data constraints, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to early growth-stage advancement. Applied to the $20M total raised as a valuation proxy, this yields an implied valuation of $38M. This single-method framework produces a range of $32M (low) to $44M (high), centered on the $38M median estimate.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M–$44M, with $38M as the point estimate. Critical uncertainties include the absence of public or private comparable companies to validate the 1.9x multiplier assumption, lack of visibility into Amperon's revenue, unit economics, or growth trajectory, and reliance on total capital raised as a valuation proxy rather than fundamental metrics. Refinement would require either peer benchmarking within infrastructure logistics or disclosure of operational metrics (ARR, customer count, burn rate) to anchor forward-looking multiples.
